p.src: The speaker later claims about $72 million from Snap and other companies in his portfolio: $V\approx \$72{,}000{,}000.$ Here we must be careful. The transcript does not cleanly say that $V$ came only from the $20,000 Snapchat investment. It says Snap and the other companies in the portfolio. A general return multiple is $M=\frac{V}{I},$ but in this case the clean multiple is uncertain because the outcome combines several holdings. The right lesson is asymmetry, not a verified ratio. A finite investment can be lost, while ownership in a successful company can produce an outcome far beyond the original salary scale.
